export const meta = {
  name: 'ajc-warning-elimination',
  description: 'Drive the 138 mechanical Lean warnings in Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge to zero, leaving only the 24 honest `declaration uses sorry` notices',
  phases: [
    { title: 'FixA', detail: 'first four file groups' },
    { title: 'FixB', detail: 'remaining file groups' },
    { title: 'Audit', detail: 'adversarial re-read of every edit' },
  ],
}

const PROJ = '/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge'

const COMMON = `
PROJECT: ${PROJ} — Lean 4 / Mathlib v4.31.0, package \`AlgebraicJacobian\`.
Your working directory is that project root; all paths below are relative to it.

GOAL: eliminate mechanical Lean lint warnings WITHOUT changing a single declaration's statement
and without weakening any proof. The project's only honest warnings are the 24
\`declaration uses \`sorry\`\` notices — leave every \`sorry\` exactly where it is.

WHERE THE WARNINGS ARE: /tmp/ajc-warm-build.log is a full green build log. Every warning line
starts with \`warning: <path>:<line>:<col>: \`. Grep YOUR files out of it first:
  grep -n "^warning: AlgebraicJacobian/<YourFile>" /tmp/ajc-warm-build.log
and read the two or three lines after each — the linter usually prints the fix.

CAUTION ON LINE NUMBERS: the copyright header of every module was normalised to a 5-line block
just before you started. For all but four files this changed no line numbers. In
Picard/TensorSectionFormula.lean, RiemannRoch/CurveBaseChange.lean and
RiemannRoch/CohomologyKit.lean everything shifted DOWN by 1 line, and in Picard/GlueDescent.lean
by 5 lines (it had no header at all). ALWAYS locate an edit by its source text, never by the
line number alone. Do not touch the header block: it is already correct.

THE FIXES, by linter (all verified against mathlib v4.31.0 conventions):
- "The \`show\` tactic should only be used to indicate intermediate goal states": replace the
  keyword \`show\` with \`change\`, keeping indentation and the rest of the line verbatim. Some are
  multi-line — change only the keyword.
- "Variable name \`x\` is not explicitly referenced": rename that binder to \`_\` (or \`_x\` when the
  name documents something). Only the flagged binder.
- "This simp argument is unused": delete exactly that argument from the \`simp\`/\`simp only\` list.
  Remove ONE argument at a time and re-check, so a breakage is attributable.
- "automatically included section variable(s) unused in theorem T": insert
  \`omit [Inst] in\` on its own line immediately above the declaration (above its docstring if it
  has one), naming exactly the instances the linter lists.
- "\`f\` does not use the following hypothesis in its type": for \`[Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]\` that
  the *statement* does not need, weaken to \`[Finite ι]\` and open the proof with \`classical\` and
  \`letI := Fintype.ofFinite ι\`. Never delete a hypothesis the statement genuinely uses.
- "Overlapping instance parameters": delete the redundant instance binders from the TOP-LEVEL
  binder list only — never from a nested hypothesis type (an induction hypothesis needs its own).
- "This line exceeds the 100 character limit": wrap it. Do not change any token.
- "has been deprecated: Use X": use X. Verify X exists by grepping
  /home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.lake-packages/mathlib.
- "try 'simp' instead of 'simpa'": replace \`simpa [..] using e\` by \`simp [..]\` only when the
  linter says so.
- "is a flexible tactic modifying ⊢": replace the bare \`simp [...]\` with the \`simp only [...]\`
  the log already prints for it; if the log does not print one, run the file through
  \`lake env lean\` with \`simp?\` in place of \`simp\` and paste the suggestion. Re-wrap to stay
  under 100 characters.
- "Definition D of class type must be marked with instance": add \`@[implicit_reducible]\` on its
  own line immediately before the definition. Do NOT convert it back to \`instance\` — these were
  deliberately demoted so that \`sorryAx\` cannot propagate through typeclass synthesis; read the
  comment above the declaration before touching it.
- "missing space in the source": e.g. \`Type (u+1)\` → \`Type (u + 1)\`.

VERIFICATION (mandatory, per file, before you report):
  lake env lean -Dpp.unicode.fun=true -DrelaxedAutoImplicit=false -DmaxSynthPendingDepth=3 \\
    -Dweak.linter.mathlibStandardSet=true AlgebraicJacobian/<YourFile>.lean
It must exit 0 and print NO warning for your file other than \`declaration uses 'sorry'\`.
(\`lake env lean\` elaborates the file against the already-built dependencies and does NOT write
to .lake/build, so you cannot invalidate anyone else's work with it. It needs several minutes
and ~7 GB for the larger files — that is expected; run it once per file, not per edit.)
If verification fails, REVERT to a state that elaborates and report exactly which fix broke it.
Never leave a file that does not elaborate.

DO NOT: edit any file outside your assigned list; run \`lake build\`; touch the lakefile; touch
anything under blueprint/; remove or prove a \`sorry\`; change a declaration's statement, name,
binders' semantics, or attributes beyond what a listed linter demands.
`

const GROUPS = [
  { key: 'gradedhilbert', files: ['Picard/GradedHilbertSerre.lean'] },
  { key: 'auslander', files: ['Albanese/AuslanderBuchsbaum.lean'] },
  { key: 'quot', files: ['Picard/QuotFunctorDef.lean', 'Picard/QuotFlatBaseChange.lean'] },
  { key: 'identity', files: ['Picard/IdentityComponent.lean'] },
  { key: 'flatness', files: ['Picard/GenericFlatnessGeometric.lean', 'Picard/EntryIdealStratum.lean'] },
  { key: 'glue', files: ['Picard/GlueDescent.lean', 'Picard/DivFunctorDef.lean'] },
  { key: 'sheaf', files: ['Picard/SheafOverEquivalence.lean', 'Picard/SectionBaseChange.lean', 'Picard/TensorSectionFormula.lean'] },
  { key: 'tail', files: ['Picard/GrassmannianCells.lean', 'Picard/RelPicFunctor.lean', 'Picard/SerreTwist.lean', 'AbelJacobi.lean', 'Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean', 'Picard/RigidPushforwardTransfer.lean', 'Albanese/AlbaneseUP.lean', 'RiemannRoch/CurveBaseChange.lean', 'RiemannRoch/CohomologyKit.lean'] },
]

const fix = (g, phaseName) => agent(`${COMMON}

YOUR FILES (fix every non-\`sorry\` warning in each, and nothing else):
${g.files.map(f => '  AlgebraicJacobian/' + f).join('\n')}

Work file by file: grep the log, read the source around each warning, apply the minimal edit,
then verify the whole file once with \`lake env lean\` as specified. Report per file: the warning
categories you fixed with counts, anything you deliberately left (with the reason), and the
verification outcome.`, { label: `fix:${g.key}`, phase: phaseName, schema: {
  type: 'object', additionalProperties: false,
  required: ['files', 'verified'],
  properties: {
    files: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', additionalProperties: false,
      required: ['file', 'fixed', 'left', 'elaborates'],
      properties: {
        file: { type: 'string' },
        fixed: { type: 'integer', description: 'number of warnings eliminated' },
        left: { type: 'string', description: 'what remains and why (sorry notices are expected)' },
        elaborates: { type: 'boolean' },
      } } },
    verified: { type: 'boolean', description: 'true iff every file above elaborated cleanly at the end' },
  },
} })

phase('FixA')
const a = await parallel(GROUPS.slice(0, 4).map(g => () => fix(g, 'FixA')))
phase('FixB')
const b = await parallel(GROUPS.slice(4).map(g => () => fix(g, 'FixB')))

const all = [...a, ...b].filter(Boolean)
const touched = all.flatMap(r => (r.files || []).map(f => f.file))

phase('Audit')
const audit = await agent(`${COMMON}

ADVERSARIAL AUDIT. Eight agents just edited these files:
${touched.map(f => '  ' + f).join('\n')}

Their reports:
${JSON.stringify(all, null, 1).slice(0, 20000)}

Do NOT trust the reports. Using the ledger diff
  git --git-dir=/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git \\
      --work-tree=/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon diff -- \\
      'MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/AlgebraicJacobian/*'
inspect EVERY hunk and answer:
1. Did any edit change a declaration's STATEMENT (binders, hypotheses, universe levels,
   conclusion) rather than only its proof or style? Instance-binder deletions and
   \`[Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]\` → \`[Finite ι]\` are statement changes — check each one is
   genuinely the weakening the linter asked for and that the proof still supplies what it needs.
2. Did any edit weaken a proof (turn a real argument into \`simp\`, drop a needed simp lemma,
   delete a hypothesis that was used)?
3. Did any \`show\` → \`change\` alter the goal? \`change\` is definitional-equality only; if the
   original \`show\` was changing the goal up to more than defeq the file would not elaborate, so
   confirm each edited file was actually re-elaborated.
4. Was any \`sorry\` removed, added, or moved?
5. Was any file outside the assigned list touched?
Report every problem you find with file:line, and FIX the ones you are sure about (you may edit
these files), re-verifying with \`lake env lean\`. Then state the residual risk plainly.`,
  { label: 'audit', phase: 'Audit' })

return { groups: all, audit }

12	## Question
13	To equip the relative Picard functor with its `AddCommGroup` (the group law
14	"tensor of line bundles") the project is building the FULL symmetric monoidal
15	category `Scheme.Modules X` (= `sheafification ∘ PresheafOfModules.Monoidal.tensorObj`),
16	which has bottomed out in the verified-absent `MonoidalClosed (PresheafOfModules R₀)`
17	(needed for the `whiskerLeft` stability of the localizing morphism property).
18	Is the full `MonoidalCategory (Scheme.Modules X)` the right Mathlib-aligned shape
19	for obtaining only the group law on LINE BUNDLES, or does Mathlib have a lighter
20	idiom that yields the `AddCommGroup` on line-bundle iso-classes WITHOUT the full
21	monoidal (let alone monoidal-closed) structure on all modules?
22	
23	## Project artifact(s)
24	- `AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/TensorObjSubstrate.lean`:113–152 — `Scheme.Modules.tensorObj`
25	  and the `monoidalCategory : MonoidalCategory X.Modules` instance (`:= sorry`).
26	- `TensorObjSubstrate.lean`:249–304 — `tensorObj_restrict_iso`, `tensorObj_isLocallyTrivial`,
27	  `exists_tensorObj_inverse` (the line-bundle cone).
28	- `TensorObjSubstrate.lean`:399–454 — `isMonoidal_W_of_whiskerLeft` /

30	  lone `whiskerLeft` fact `W g → W (F ◁ g)` for ALL `F`.
31	- `RelPicFunctor.lean`:235–269 — the `addCommGroup` sorry the cone discharges.
32	- `LineBundlePullback.lean`:115–131 — `IsLocallyTrivial` (the project's self-described
33	  "stand-in for the missing Mathlib `IsInvertible` predicate") and `OnProduct` carrier.
34	
35	## Decisions identified
36	
37	### Decision A: full `MonoidalCategory (Scheme.Modules X)` (→ `MonoidalClosed (PresheafOfModules R₀)`) as the substrate for the group law
38	
39	- **Mathlib idiom**. Mathlib's Picard group is `CommRing.Pic R := Shrink (Skeleton (SemimoduleCat R))ˣ`
40	  with the `CommGroup` transported from `Units` of the skeleton `CommMonoid`
41	  (`Mathlib.RingTheory.PicardGroup`, `CommRing.Pic` def:407, `instCommGroupPic`:412;
42	  `CategoryTheory.Skeleton.instCommMonoid` from `Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Skeleton`).
43	  The invertibility carrier is a **Prop predicate** `Module.Invertible R M`
44	  (PicardGroup.lean:78), NOT a bundled monoidal object. Crucially the monoidal
45	  category underlying the skeleton there is `ModuleCat R` over a **fixed** ring
46	  (`ModuleCat.monoidalCategory`, `ModuleCat.MonoidalCategory.symmetricCategory`,
47	  `Mathlib.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Monoidal.{Basic,Symmetric}`) — which needs **no**
48	  sheafification, localization, or `MonoidalClosed`.
49	- **Project's path**. Build `MonoidalCategory` on ALL quasi-coherent modules
50	  `Scheme.Modules X`, whose only remaining gap is `whiskerLeft : W g → W (F ◁ g)`
51	  for an ARBITRARY presheaf-of-modules `F`, provable (à la Mathlib's
52	  `GrothendieckTopology.W.whiskerLeft`) only through `MonoidalClosed (PresheafOfModules R₀)`
53	  — verified absent and a multi-file Mathlib-PR-scale build.
54	- **Gap**: divergent-with-cost (over-building). The consumer (`RelPicFunctor`
55	  `addCommGroup`) only ever tensors **line bundles** (`IsLocallyTrivial`, locally free
56	  rank 1). Line bundles are **flat** — in Mathlib, `Module.Invertible R M` already
57	  yields `instance : Module.Finite`, `instance : Projective` (PicardGroup.lean:195–196),

60	  (`Module.Flat.lTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap`, used in PicardGroup.lean:205–207;
61	  packaged as `Module.Invertible.lTensor_bijective_iff`, PicardGroup.lean:223–229), and
62	  `⊗` is always right-exact so it preserves surjectivity. So the ENTIRE reason the project

64	  once the scope is the flat/line-bundle subcategory. The directive's "elementwise exactness

72	- **Verdict**: ALIGN_WITH_MATHLIB — abandon the all-modules monoidal-closed route; build the
73	  group law on the line-bundle (flat) subcategory, where `whiskerLeft`/`tensorObj_restrict_iso`

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Drive the de-umbrella campaign wave by wave over the project import DAG.
#
#   scripts/deumbrella-wave.sh [max_waves] [parallel_jobs]
#
# A module's minimal-import probe is only CORRECT once every module in its
# transitive project-import closure is already umbrella-free: while a dependency
# still says `import Mathlib`, it hands the whole of Mathlib to the importer and
# the linter reports every Mathlib module as redundant.  So each wave converts
# exactly the bare modules whose project dependencies are already clean, rebuilds
# them so the next wave's probes see the narrowed oleans, and repeats.
#
# Wave 1 is the DAG sources (no project imports at all).  Failures are restored
# by scripts/deumbrella.sh and simply stay bare, blocking their dependents until
# a human or a later run handles them.
set -uo pipefail

MAX_WAVES=${1:-99}
JOBS=${2:-6}
HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
cd "$HERE/.."

ready_modules () {
python3 - <<'PY'
import os, re
mods = {}
for dp, _, fns in os.walk('AlgebraicJacobian'):
    for fn in fns:
        if fn.endswith('.lean'):
            p = os.path.join(dp, fn)
            mods[p[:-5].replace('/', '.')] = p
imports, umbrella = {}, set()
for n, p in mods.items():
    ds = []
    for line in open(p, errors='replace'):
        m = re.match(r'^import\s+([A-Za-z0-9_.]+)', line)
        if m:
            d = m.group(1)
            if d == 'Mathlib':
                umbrella.add(n)
            elif d.startswith('AlgebraicJacobian'):
                ds.append(d)
    imports[n] = ds
memo = {}
def contaminated(m):
    if m in memo:
        return memo[m]
    memo[m] = True
    r = m in umbrella or any(contaminated(d) for d in imports.get(m, []))
    memo[m] = r
    return r
ready = [m for m in umbrella if not any(contaminated(d) for d in imports[m])]
# cheapest first: a failure then costs the least, and the early wins land sooner
ready.sort(key=lambda m: os.path.getsize(mods[m]))
for m in ready:
    print(mods[m])
PY
}

wave=0
while [ "$wave" -lt "$MAX_WAVES" ]; do
  wave=$((wave + 1))
  mapfile -t READY < <(ready_modules)
  [ "${#READY[@]}" -eq 0 ] && { echo "== no module is ready; stopping after $((wave - 1)) wave(s)"; break; }

  echo "== wave $wave: ${#READY[@]} module(s) ready"
  printf '%s\n' "${READY[@]}" | xargs -P "$JOBS" -I{} bash "$HERE/deumbrella.sh" {}

  # Rebuild the converted modules so the next wave probes against narrowed oleans.
  targets=()
  for f in "${READY[@]}"; do
    grep -qx 'import Mathlib' "$f" || targets+=("${f%.lean}")
  done
  [ "${#targets[@]}" -eq 0 ] && { echo "== wave $wave converted nothing; stopping"; break; }
  echo "== wave $wave: rebuilding ${#targets[@]} module(s)"
  lake build "${targets[@]//\//.}" || echo "!! rebuild reported failures in wave $wave"
done

echo "== bare \`import Mathlib\` modules remaining: $(grep -rlx 'import Mathlib' AlgebraicJacobian --include=*.lean | wc -l)"

## Current (false) statement

> Let `k` be a field of characteristic 0, `B` a finite-type `k`-algebra that is
> standard smooth of relative dimension `n`, and `b ∈ B` with `D_{B/k} b = 0`.

## Why it is false

`IsStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension n k B` means only "`B` admits a submersive
presentation of relative dimension `n`" — it implies `Ω[B/k]` is locally free of
rank `n`, but imposes **no connectedness**, and crucially no **geometric**

21	Define a rational map `Φ : V × V ⇢ G`, `(x, y) ↦ φ(x)·φ(y)⁻¹`. More precisely, if `(U, φ_U)`
22	represents `φ`, then `Φ` is represented by
23	```
24	U × U --(φ_U × φ_U)--> G × G --(id × inv)--> G × G --m--> G.
25	```
26	Clearly `Φ` is defined at a diagonal point `(x, x)` if `φ` is defined at `x`, and then
27	`Φ(x, x) = e`. Conversely, if `Φ` is defined at `(x, x)`, then it is defined on an open
28	neighbourhood of `(x, x)`; in particular there is an open `U ⊆ V` such that `Φ` is defined on
29	`{x} × U`. After possibly replacing `U` by a smaller open subset (not necessarily containing `x`),
30	`φ` will be defined on `U`. For `u ∈ U`, the formula `φ(x) = Φ(x, u)·φ(u)` defines `φ` at `x`.
31	Thus **`φ` is defined at `x` iff `Φ` is defined at `(x, x)`.**

33	The rational map `Φ` defines a map `Φ* : 𝒪_{G,e} → k(V × V)`. Since `Φ` sends `(x, x)` to `e` if
34	it is defined there, `Φ` is defined at `(x, x)` **iff `Im(𝒪_{G,e}) ⊆ 𝒪_{V×V,(x,x)}`.**

ADDENDUM 3's second corrigendum left one question: the no-go's argument is degree-agnostic, but
its only exhibited witness (`F = tX² + XY + tY²` over `k[t]`, `C = P¹`, `π = id`) has degree 2 on a
curve of genus 0, off the stratum the functor pins. At `g = 0` the no-go is vacuous, at `g = 1`
the base can be shrunk to confine, and at `g ≥ 2` nobody had exhibited anything. This addendum
settles it, corrects the argument ADDENDUM 3 used for shrink-stability, and — the part that
actually decides the route — gives a sharp iff for R1.

### 4.1 First, the criterion ADDENDUM 3 used is the wrong one

ADDENDUM 3 argued shrink-stability as "the divisor stays irreducible over every nonempty open of
the base, so no Zariski shrink evades the no-go". That is true of the exhibited family and it is
not the right criterion, because `IsLocallyCertified` (`Picard/DivisorFamilyZar.lean:71`) asks for
a **span-⊤ family**, i.e. a *cover* — and a cover cannot delete a point. The correct criterion is

> (★) there is a point `s ∈ Spec R` such that for **every** open `U ∋ s`, some connected component
> of `supp(D|_U)` meets both `π⁻¹(p₀)` and `π⁻¹(p₁)`.

Under the criterion ADDENDUM 3 actually stated, the campaign's own genus-0 example would be
*evaded*: the two witness points of `tX² + XY + tY²` are `([1:0], 0)` and `([0:1], 0)`, both lying
over `t = 0`, and over `t ≠ 0` the roots are `(−1 ± √(1−4t²))/2t`, which are never `0` or `∞`. So
`D` restricted to `𝔸¹ ∖ {0}` misses *both* pinned fibres. It is a genuine counterexample only
because a cover must contain `t = 0`. The conclusion was right; half the reason was missing.

### 4.2 The reduction (general — no hypotheses on `k`, `C`, `π`, `n`)

Let `S = supp D ⊆ C ×_k Spec R`. Since `D` is finite flat of degree `n` over `R`, `S → Spec R` is
finite, hence closed. For `c ∈ P¹(k)` set `W_c :=` the image in `Spec R` of `S ∩ (π⁻¹(c) × Spec R)`
— a closed subset. Then for `s ∈ Spec R`:

* `s ∉ W_c` ⟹ `U := Spec R ∖ W_c` is an open neighbourhood of `s` on which `supp(D|_U)` misses
  `π⁻¹(c)` entirely, i.e. `D|_U` is confined to the chart complementary to `π⁻¹(c)`;
* `s ∈ W_c` ⟹ *every* `U ∋ s` has `supp(D|_U)` meeting `π⁻¹(c)`.

And `s ∈ W_c ⟺ supp(D_s)` meets `π⁻¹(c)`, a purely **fibrewise** condition. Since `D_s` is finite
